description.narrative:
Stakeholders impact:
Increased access to MSME and climate finance: The MSME sector is extremely critical for the development of the country and provides jobs to over 110 million people. Moreover, addressing climate change holistically and improving crisis resilience is important, and India requires access to substantial funding in order to meet its committed NDCs, to reduce the emissions intensity of its GDP significantly by the year 2030. The proposed investment would support the Bank in increasing funding to MSMEs and towards climate finance.
Market impact:
Beyond the project, IFC expects that this investment will promote greater resilience in the market via innovation, demonstration, and replication channels. This approach is expected to demonstrate the viability of MSME and climate lending and encourage other Financial Institutions to follow suit.

The proposed project comprises a primary equity investment in Federal Bank Limited (FBL or the Bank), the seventh largest private sector bank in India, for up to INR9.84 billion (approximately US$120 million equivalent), by International Finance Corporation (IFC), IFC Financial Institutions Growth Fund, LP (FIG), and IFC Emerging Asia Fund, LP (EAF). The primary equity will strengthen the Banks Tier 1 capital adequacy ratio, which will allow it to accelerate its lending, including to MSMEs and for climate finance. The investment will support the Banks commitment to financial inclusion and support it operationalize its strong commitment to sustainability and climate finance. The proposed transaction is subject to all required approvals.
